subject: toucan
pitch: A keel-billed toucan showing off on a short mossy branch. A huge rainbow beak in lime green, sky blue and orange with a cherry-red tip, a glossy black body, a lemon-yellow bib, a ring of lime-green skin around each eye, bright blue feet and a scarlet patch under the tail. A single pink orchid blooms on the branch beside it.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the toucan's proportions and its perch on the branch, working out the key heights and positions so the bird sits naturally above the floor.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a root hips joint, then a spine chain curving up through the chest toward the neck and head, followed by a separate neck chain connecting to the head joint, making sure joint names stay unique across chains.

For the body, I'm sweeping a tube along that spine-to-neck path using the catmull-rom curve through the key points, varying the radii to taper from a wider belly to a narrower neck, and planning a glossy black material for the plumage.

For the bib, instead of wrestling with sector angles on a curved tube, I'll switch to a paint function that marks a region as yellow when the surface normal faces forward and the height falls within the chest/throat band, leaving everything else black — keeping the edges hard rather than blended.

Working out the eye geometry now: a flattened lime ring sphere positioned on each side of the head, with a smaller dark pupil sphere protruding from it plus a tiny highlight, scaling the ring thin along the x-axis to get the right disc shape.

For the beak I'm planning a large curved loft shape, roughly 0.17 long and 0.05 high at the base, built from stations along a bezier curve for the upper mandible's downward curve. I'm mapping out the keel-billed toucan's real coloring -- lime green top ridge, orange sides, blue lower base, and a cherry red tip -- and plan to paint these as bands along the beak's length parameter.

Working out the paint logic now: using the position along the beak plus the angle around its circumference to decide lime vs orange vs blue vs red, with a near-black ring at the very base where the mandibles meet.

Switching to a swept-path approach for the beak instead of a loft, curving the upper mandible forward and slightly downward with tapering elliptical radii from base to tip.

Checking that upper and lower mandible meet closely at the jaw joint and taper correctly to a near-closed tip, nudging the lower tip position slightly for a believable gap. I'll also add small dark nostril dots near the base of the upper beak for detail.

Now I'm sketching the head joint sphere's position and scale, then moving to the folded wings—planning a joint chain running from shoulder down the body side to a tapered tip, defining their rest-pose coordinates.

For the wing shape itself, I'm working out an extruded teardrop outline in the side-view plane, defining the shoulder anchor point and relative outline coordinates that will form the wing's silhouette.

I'm working out the tail position hanging down behind the perched toucan's body, making sure it clears the branch and feet, then positioning the wing as a shoulder-jointed extrusion along the back.

Writing wing bone chain...

For coloring, I'm thinking wings should be a slightly bluer black than the body, and considering whether to add small white/yellow rump markings and a scarlet undertail patch typical of toucans, adjusting the body sweep points to accommodate these features.

Now I'm working out the tail construction as a chain of joints following a sweep path curving backward and down, with flattened radii to give it a wide, thin shape, and figuring out the correct normal direction for the tube so it orients naturally with the tail's downward curve.

Next I'm sketching the leg chains with blue feet: short joints from the hip down through a knee joint to the foot, positioning them so the visible tarsus runs from mid-body height down to near the floor level while keeping the thighs hidden beneath the body sweep.

Now I'm working out the zygodactyl toes—two forward, two back—since the branch runs along the x-axis, the toes should spread perpendicular to it (along z) so the foot appears to wrap and grip the branch naturally, each toe modeled as a thin rod from the foot center outward.

I need to keep the toe joint count manageable while making sure the toe tips curve downward enough to visually clasp the branch without actually poking through its surface geometry, since the branch radius means tips at z=±0.05 could penetrate the branch if positioned too low.

I'll skip the claw spikes for efficiency and focus on the branch itself: sweeping it along a curved path with varying radius, then texturing it with a mottled brown-and-moss paint combined with countershading so the top looks mossy and the underside darker, making sure the branch geometry touches the ground plane.

I'm placing the toe base and ankle positions around the branch, then adding scattered moss clumps as small flattened spheres across the branch surface, a short tapering side twig with a few leaf cards, and a pink orchid positioned near the toucan on the branch.

For the orchid, I'm working out a single stem curving up from the branch to a bloom facing forward, built from pointed sepal and petal shapes plus a darker magenta labellum lip.

Still writing petal geometry...

I'm layering sepals, petals, and lip at slightly offset depths for a 3D effect, then setting the color palette: pink petals, lighter pink sepals, deep pink lip, yellow center column, with tiny dark spots.

Computing the tilt orientation so the flower faces forward and slightly upward, then sweeping a stem curve from the branch point up to the flower center with a small green radius.

Still positioning the leaves... Now I'm thinking about the toucan's rest pose for "showing off" -- puffed chest, slightly tilted head, possibly an open beak rather than neutral closed jaw.

Keeping the head pitched up a bit with wings slightly spread away from the body, tips offset outward for an open posture. I'm working out how the neck's body-sweep path merges smoothly into the head sphere, checking that the radii and positions line up so the transition looks seamless.

Now I'm defining the body's skeleton path with curve points running from hips up through the chest, tapering radii along the way, then building a spine chain parented to the hips and a separate neck chain that connects off the spine's upper joint.

Refining the yellow/black color conditions for the head sphere, keeping the sides black while the throat and beak base stay yellow, plus adding a thin white fringe near the bib edge...

I'm also adding a thin red band for the toucan's lower belly line, and sketching the beak's paint function with color zones -- green top, orange sides, blue base for a layered mandible look.

I'm tallying the color palette to keep it under the limit, then positioning the eye as a dark sphere nested within the lime ring on the head, checking the offsets so it protrudes slightly without clipping.

Now I'm placing the eye highlight as a tiny white sphere, then working out the wing attachment point relative to the body radius at that cross-section to make sure the wing plate sits flush against the torso with a slight outward spread.

Calculating wing bone chain joints...

Adding radiating feather ridge lines using angle-based striping, then thinking about a yellow-white rump patch near the tail to match the keel-billed toucan's coloring.

Now I'm working out the leg joint hierarchy—positioning hips under the belly, then placing knee and ankle points to form the leg sweep, tapering the radius for a trouser-like feathered effect.

Next I'm figuring out the toe chains branching off each ankle, setting forward-facing toe tip positions with left/right naming conventions.

The branch also sits under the toucan's feet. I'm adding a small side twig sprouting off the branch with a couple of simple leaf shapes, then scattering flattened moss clumps across the branch surface using a randomized filter so moss only appears on upward-facing areas.

I'm alternating moss colors between a few greens and using a low-poly icosahedron for the stick geometry, while excluding the area near the toucan's feet from the scatter so moss doesn't overlap there. Now I'm positioning the orchid on the opposite side of the toucan.

Working out the orchid's stem curve and flower placement, with the center point and orientation vectors determining how the flower faces forward and slightly upward.

Now I'm laying out the petal structure: dorsal and lateral sepals positioned at specific angles, rounder lateral petals, a magenta lip, and a tiny yellow column sphere marking the center.

Writing petal geometry code...

Still positioning leaves...

Actually since everything needs a bone binding, I'll set up a simple rig: a root joint with a branch joint beneath it, and attach all the prop parts—orchid, leaf, stick—to that branch joint rather than any toucan bone.

Working out the toucan's joint assignments now, making sure head, neck, legs, and tail each bind to their correct bone rather than defaulting to the nearest joint incorrectly. Mapping out the tail's curve as a chain of points descending from the body.

Now I'm defining the tail's tapering sweep shape with a wide feathered base narrowing toward the tip, painted black, and placing a reddish undertail patch where the tail meets the body.

I'm figuring out the scarlet patch's exact position and size using two small spheres to mimic covert feathers, then double-checking overall body height against the beak placement and handling details like nostril placement via surface raycasting and a subtle ridge line along the beak's top edge.

Now I'm defining the radius function for the upper beak's taper, adjusting the base dimensions since my first attempt made it too tall relative to the body proportions.

Still refining beak taper dimensions...

Now I'm setting up the jaw joint and head joint hierarchy, then starting the neck chain using a short catmull spline between two points parented to the spine.

I'm confirming the imports needed—builder, rng, catmull, bezier, paint, gradient utilities—and naming the spine chain joints with spine roles. I'm also laying out the paint scheme with countershaded back and belly using mottled textures in moss and bark tones.

Writing leg chain code...

Still defining toe geometry and claw spikes...

For the twig, I'm sweeping a curved path off the branch with tapering radius and round caps, colored with the bark texture, then adding extruded leaf shapes at the end. Now I'm writing a body paint function that colors the belly red near the top and lemon yellow below, with black elsewhere.

Checking that this same paint function works correctly across the head sphere and face too — the cheeks should read yellow while the eyes stay clear based on their surface normal angles. Now I'm writing a helper to rotate point arrays by an angle for the orchid petal outlines.

Writing rotation math...

Then I'm figuring out the extrusion call for the petal, making sure the x/y basis vectors stay perpendicular, and starting to sketch out the more complex lip shape geometry.

I decide to skip the side lobes and extra details like whiskers and spots, keeping the lip simple with just the main shape in magenta. I settle on a thin stem radius and decide to skip adding a bud since the scene only needs a single bloom, then start laying out the stem's path coordinates.
